newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila sees $200-350 mln exports fron nickel mine.
newsitem.headline: Manila sees $200-350 mln exports fron nickel mine.

text.p: The Philippines expects yearly exports of $200 to $350 million when production resumes at the rehabilitated Nonoc nickel mine in 1998, a government official said on Monday.
Nonoc was one of the world's 10 biggest nickel refineries, capable of annual production of 65 million pounds of nickel until it ceased operations in 1986.

Asset Privatisation Trust executive trustee Gonzalo Santos said new investors will start rehabilitation work on the Nonoc refinery late this year with the signing of a definitive agreement last weekend over its sale to Pacific Nickel Holdings Ltd.

Australian explorer Arboyne NL, through its option to acquire all of the share capital of Pacific Nickel, has said it planned to rehabilitate the Nonoc laterite nickel operation at a cost of US$370 million.
Pacific Nickel has agreed to pay the Philippine government $264 million for the acquisition of Nonoc on an installment basis. It will also pay $70 million to creditors.

Arboyne's resource estimate of recoverable ore remaining at Nonoc and adjacent to the 60 hectare refinery was 39 million tonnes containing an average of 1.28 percent nickel, 0.12 percent cobalt and 38.2 percent iron.
